tagline: Suisei played IG Arena Nagoya and closes the tour in Fukuoka in three days; Nagao Kei organized NIJISANJI's Splatoon tournament and his team won it; hololive booked Korea and Texas for December on the same weekend; and the Streamer Awards ceremony is 72 hours out.
inThisIssue: Hoshimachi Suisei at IG Arena Nagoya — third of four tour stops; Fukuoka finale November 12 with global cinema live viewing via Event Cinemas and LVE
Neochi Samba wins NIJISANJI Ikamatsuri 2026 — organizer Nagao Kei's four-person squad takes the championship in the 96-liver Splatoon 3 tournament

lead.title: Hoshimachi Suisei plays IG Arena Nagoya — third of four; Once Upon a Stellar tour closes November 12 at Marine Messe Fukuoka Hall A with global cinema live viewing confirmed
lead.body: Hoshimachi Suisei played IG Arena (Aichi International Arena) in Nagoya on November 7, the third of four cities on her HOSHIMACHI SUISEI ARENA TOUR 2026 Once Upon a Stellar. Doors opened at 5:00 PM JST, start at 6:00 PM. The show was simulcast on ZAIKO for viewers who could not attend. The tour opened at K Arena Yokohama on September 8-9, then moved to GLION Arena in Kobe on October 21, and now has one stop remaining: Marine Messe Fukuoka Hall A on November 12. The Fukuoka finale is the only stop with a confirmed global cinema live viewing — via Event Cinemas in Australia and Live Viewing Entertainment (LVE) internationally — scheduled at 19:00 JST on Thursday. Studio STELLAR, Suisei's personal management company launched earlier this year while she continues as a hololive member, booked the four-city run. IG Arena in Nagoya (Aichi International Arena) holds approximately 15,000 for concerts; Marine Messe Fukuoka Hall A seats approximately 10,000. The four-city Once Upon a Stellar run is the largest consecutive arena tour in Suisei's career.

stories.title: Nagao Kei's team Neochi Samba wins NIJISANJI Ikamatsuri 2026 — tournament organizer and three teammates take the championship in the 96-liver Splatoon 3 bracket
stories.blurb: The fifth Nurimakure! Nijisanji Ikamatsuri ran November 7-8 on NIJISANJI's official YouTube, putting 96 livers across 24 teams through a round-robin and double-elimination bracket in Splatoon 3. The championship went to Neochi Samba — the team built around tournament organizer Nagao Kei, joined by Koshimizu Toru, Umi Shifu, and Sofia Valentine. Runner-up was Yusho Koho(w); third went to Isumya, Zenbu Yatte; fourth to Zettai Yusho Drops. The 2026 edition is the tournament's largest field to date at 96 participants. Nagao Kei is the event's creator and organizer. His team won. Stream archives are on participant channels and the main NIJISANJI YouTube.

stories.title: hololive production books AGF 2026 in South Korea and Anime Frontier Fort Worth for the same December 4-6 weekend — Dreams booth, fan experiences, talent stages
stories.blurb: COVER Corporation confirmed two December fan events in a single week. On November 2, the company announced that hololive Dreams — the rhythm-RPG for iOS, Android, and Steam featuring 54 hololive talents — will have a booth at AGF 2026 at Ilsan KINTEX in South Korea from December 4-6, with playable mini-games, live talent stage appearances, and exclusive giveaways. On November 6, the company confirmed hololive Meet returns to Anime Frontier at Fort Worth Convention Center in Texas for December 4-6, with exclusive fan experiences. The simultaneous booking in East Asia and North America runs the same weekend as AFA Singapore and DreamHack Stockholm on November 27-29, making two back-to-back double-market weekends to close the year.

stories.title: NIJISANJI Girls Idol Festival Osaka Dec 19-20 — on-site general tickets open November 14; streaming tickets on Niconico November 19; 16 performers across two stages
stories.blurb: NIJISANJI Girls Idol Festival at INTEX Osaka Hall 5 opens its general on-site ticket sales November 14, with Niconico Live streaming tickets following on November 19. The two-day event features 16 performers: Iris Stage on December 19 (Mito Tsukino, Rena Yorumi, Ratna Petit, Karuta Yamagami, Nozomi Ishigami, Meruto Kuramochi, Ruri Shioriha, Toto Tatsuden) and Prism Stage on December 20 (Lize Helesta, Lulu Suzuhara, Kokoro Amamiya, Rika Igarashi, Riko Shiga, Tamako Kirara, Berry Saotome, Suzuna Nanase). First revealed at the NijiFes 2026 closing ceremony, the festival runs in parallel with JR Central's Oshi Tabi Shinkansen campaign through January 31, 2027.

stories.title: 2026 Streamer Awards ceremony is November 12 in Los Angeles — Best VTuber result sealed; nominees TheBurntPeanut, Ironmouse, Koseki Bijou, Crelly, Gigi Murin
stories.blurb: The 2026 Streamer Awards ceremony airs November 12 in Los Angeles — QTCinderella hosts, red carpet 2:30 PM PT, main show 5:30 PM PT. Best VTuber voting closed October 31 with no live tally visible to voters; the result stays sealed until ceremony night. The five nominees are TheBurntPeanut (back-to-back defending champion), Ironmouse, Koseki Bijou, Crelly, and Gigi Murin. TheBurntPeanut unveiled a joke redesign of his peanut avatar with long orange hair mid-October after community calls for him to withdraw over past comments distancing himself from the VTuber label; the category legitimacy debate ran through voting close and enters ceremony week unresolved.

indieSubhead: NO AGENCY, NO PROBLEM — NEWS FROM THE SELF-MADE CORNER OF THE SCENE

indies.title: SpacePrinceEdenVT debuts November 3 — opens the November indie class; CrazyTama and Lucieliya up next on the 11th
indies.blurb: Independent VTuber SpacePrinceEdenVT held their debut stream on November 3, opening the November indie calendar. Per hololist.net, CrazyTama and Lucieliya debut on November 11, Cassian Aetheria on November 16, and Leannleo on November 21. The November window is unusually active for ambient viewer traffic: the Streamer Awards ceremony on the 12th, the Shattered Legends premiere window, and the Suisei Fukuoka finale all draw crossover audiences in the same two weeks, giving debuts launched now a wider reach than a typical November slot.

indies.title: Philippine indie VTubers pandorawasthere and kaheru_orange appear at AME Matsuri 2026 — UP Diliman; BY THE BEAT lands a Mall of Asia outdoor ad
indies.blurb: Independent VTubers @pandorawasthere and @kaheru_orange appeared at AME Matsuri 2026 at the University of the Philippines Diliman on November 6, per VTuber NewsDrop, continuing the pattern of Southeast Asian campus conventions serving as fan meetup spaces for regional indie VTubers. Separately this week, fans placed an advertisement for independent VTuber BY THE BEAT on the Mall of Asia ad globe — described by VTuber NewsDrop as a first outdoor placement of this scale for that talent. Fan-funded billboard and ad campaigns for indie VTubers have accelerated as a grassroots visibility tool across Southeast Asia and East Asia through 2025-2026.

tea.text: The /vt/ Streamer Awards thread opened its election-night format on November 7, five days early. The operating theory is that the five-day runway is necessary to process the full range of predicted outcomes before any outcome is confirmed. The thread is running three parallel tracks: a bracket predicting who beats who in a head-to-head, an hourly poll running since October 31 that everyone acknowledges is not the official vote, and a contingency post preparing the response to send if TheBurntPeanut wins again. The contingency post is currently 2,100 words. Someone pointed out it is longer than any acceptance speech in Streamer Awards history. The thread is treating this as a data point, not a critique. The ceremony is in three days. The thread considers itself ready.

The Nijisanji Ikamatsuri bracket-rigging theory arrived on /vt/ twelve minutes after the Neochi Samba win was confirmed. The core argument is that Nagao Kei organized the event, wrote the team assignment rules, and ran the bracket, and that his team won, and that these facts together form a structure that is at minimum suggestive. The counter-argument is that there are 24 teams in a double-elimination bracket and even with favorable seeding the wins still have to happen on the field. The original poster acknowledged this. The thread responded that acknowledging this is not the same as caring about it. Nagao Kei posted a thank-you to everyone who participated. The theory thread quoted the thank-you post and filed it under the category suspicious.

The Shattered Legends premiere date thread is on day 27 since the mid-November window was announced. The methodology has evolved into a system where every post from the five cast members and Matthew Mercer is run through a heuristic: does it contain a date, an expression of excitement that could be premiere-adjacent, or a suspiciously long gap in social activity. Posts with no content are logged as a gap and treated as evidence of prep. Posts with content are logged as filler and treated as concealment. Matthew Mercer posted about an unrelated Critical Role project on November 6 and the thread flagged it as concealment. It has been 27 days. Mid-November has twelve days left. The thread is not concerned.

Word on /vt/ is that the Phase Connect Filian situation has entered a new phase: the community has stopped debating whether the debut happens and started debating what category of event it falls into when it does. Options under active discussion include a standard corporate debut, a soft launch with no formal announcement, a stealth debut at an unusually late hour with minimal lead time, and what one poster described as a full theatrical comeback with a countdown page and four teaser trailers. The thread is assigning probability estimates. The stealth-debut option is currently running second. First place is a scenario labeled the door just opens one day and she is streaming and nobody scheduled this. The thread considers all scenarios equally plausible. No timeline is attached to any of them.

footerNote: Next signal drops Monday, 16 November — after the Fukuoka finale, after the Streamer Awards, and somewhere in the week that Shattered Legends is supposed to begin. November 12 is going to be a lot. See you on the other side.
